summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (94/191)

data.turoyo: <...> kito hən mu sawal, i naqqa i ḥalawto, d koḥəlwo i tərto aw i ʕezo aw i ʕwono, lo kobi u ḥalwaṯṯe kule, hul d lo maḏ̣iri u saxlaṯṯe aʕlayye. <...>
data.translation: <...> Bei manchen Tieren gibt die Kuh, die Ziege oder das Schaf, wenn die Melkerin sie melkt, nicht ihre ganze Milch her, ehe man nicht ihre Muttergefühle dadurch anregt, daß man ihr Junges unter sie stellt. <...>

rationale: First indexed III Infectum example: extract the maḏ̣iri clause already embedded in the inherited Preterit quotation, not a new independent attestation.

before: (ʕal) das Junge zum Saugen unter das Muttertier stellen, damit es Milch gibt;
after: (ʕal) das Junge zum Saugen unter das Muttertier stellen, damit es Milch gibt, ohne das Junge tatsächlich saugen zu lassen;
rationale: 94/192 explicitly states that the women prevent actual suckling; the operation induces milk flow rather than feeding the young. Preserve the inherited government notation and narrow only this ambiguity.

summary: The operation has an implicit human handler, the young as a zero-marked object and the mother animal as aʕlayye, with ʕal-. It is distinct from the homonym meaning harm.
94/191 contrasts Infectum maḏ̣iri in a limiting clause and Preterit maḏ̣ərre in a completed-condition clause. Both are in one already published passage, not independent evidence from separate texts.

The definition at 94/192 explicitly says the young wants to suck but the women prevent it; the mother nonetheless responds and can be milked. This motivates a semantic clarification of the inherited gloss.
Infinitiv teḏ̣iro names this established technical procedure. No separate new technical sense or fixed idiom is established.
